adjudicated.jp: 「金曜日、か」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Friday, then."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 世界が揺り戻されるまで、あと三日ほど。
adjudicated.en: There remain three days to the swingback of the world.
comments: Including this day. Uh, for those who can't do basic math, which I suspect is most of you. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 揺り戻される describes the world being reset, rolled back, or snapping back. 'Swingback' is not a natural noun for this event.

adjudicated.jp: 記憶がなくなって全てリセットされて。
adjudicated.en: Memories will be gone, and all will be reset.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ……うそ寒い。
adjudicated.en: ...a bit chilling.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: それは死ぬことと大差ないのではないかとも思う。
adjudicated.en: That, I think, just may not be significantly different from death.
comments: More hints that the week should be a day, see CCA0017A -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: この一週間は、誌面の記録にしか残されない。
adjudicated.en: Of this one week there will be nothing left but a written report.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺がそれを思い返すことはない。
adjudicated.en: I will never be able to think again about any of this.
comments: And also, to change his mind. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 決して。
adjudicated.en: Never.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 昔。
adjudicated.en: Once upon a time,
comments: At the very least let's pay lip service to the time loop. It could be ten thousand years before for all the inattentive reader knows. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 昔 simply locates the memory in the past. 'Once upon a time' adds a fairy-tale storytelling formula.

adjudicated.jp: こんなゲームで遊んだ。
adjudicated.en: there was this videogame I played.
comments: Absolute first (of TWO) times he's referencing playing videogames. Despite him knowing eroge tropes perfectly. And never being shown to have the time or the inclination to play videogames at the mansion. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ロープレ。
adjudicated.en: Role playing.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 舞台は未来。
adjudicated.en: Setting is futuristic.
adjudicated.assessment: The count noun requires an article or possessive: 'The setting is futuristic' or 'Its setting is the future.'

adjudicated.jp: 世界は荒廃し、人々はドーム都市で生きている。
adjudicated.en:
The outside world devastated, people live
in domed cities.
comments: ...hum, technically it's just domed *farmlands*, but I suppose it's irrelevant. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 野生動物はモンスター化し、人を襲う。
adjudicated.en:
Wild animals have turned into monsters and
attack the people.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 主人公はモンスターハンター。
adjudicated.en: The protagonist is a monster hunter.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 日常的なクエストから、やがては世界を支配する存在との戦いへ。
adjudicated.en:
It starts with ordinary quests, then eventually
ends in a fight with the being that rules the
world.
comments: See CCA0010. Likely not intended to be the same game... or is it? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ロープレでは普通、キャラクターが戦闘で敗北すると、魔法や科学等で蘇生させられる。
adjudicated.en:
In typical RPGs, when characters are defeated in
battle, they can be revived with some magic or
some technological gadget.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 主人公は何度死のうが主人公であり、パーティーが全滅してゲームオーバーにならない限り、危機的な破滅は起こらない。
adjudicated.en:
The protagonist can die as many times as he wants,
but he's the main character; within the limit of
the party not being entirely eliminated, causing
a game over, no complete failure will occur.
adjudicated.assessment: The protagonist remains the protagonist however many times he dies; the source does not grant him a desire or choice to die. The rest of the sentence has a malformed 'within the limit of' condition and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text: The protagonist can die as many times as he wants

adjudicated.jp: 当然、主観記憶は保持される。
adjudicated.en: Naturally, subjective memories would be preserved.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ところがコイツは違った。
adjudicated.en: Turns out, this one was different.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 主人公のみならず、キャラクターが死ぬと、それは厳然たる死なのである。
adjudicated.en:
Not just when the main character dies, but if
any character dies, that death is the final kind.
adjudicated.assessment: 厳然たる死 means an uncompromisingly real or irrevocable death. 'The final kind' is vague and does not state what distinguishes it; intrusive engine line breaks remain.

highlights.text: that death is the final kind

adjudicated.jp: 他の仲間は都市まで戻り、死亡者のクローンをセーブポイントも兼ねる施設に要請する。
adjudicated.en:
The other members have to make it back to the
city, and request a clone of the deceased from
the facility that also serves as save point.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 直前のセーブデータ時の主人公が、そこではポンと精製される。
adjudicated.en:
And pop, the protagonist was restored to just
before the data was saved.
adjudicated.assessment: The facility produces the protagonist as he existed at the most recent save data. The English places the restored state immediately before that save, shifting the checkpoint backward.

highlights.text:
And pop, the protagonist was restored to just
before the data was saved.

adjudicated.jp: そして誰も何も疑問に思うことなく、冒険は続くのだ。
adjudicated.en:
And then, without even thinking to question
anything or anyone, the adventure continues.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ショックだった。
adjudicated.en: I was shocked.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: セーブ以降の、死んだ主人公の固有時間は、まったく省みられない。
adjudicated.en:
The protagonist's eigentime after the save and
before death was never ever re-examinable.
comments: Let's start throwing in semi-credible mathematical spatial concepts... not that this doesn't fit in the big giant troll this all is, since he's literally pointing a giant spotlight on how people's memories should be erased but aren't. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The dead protagonist's own elapsed experience after the save is not considered or honored at all. 'Re-examinable' means capable of later inspection and changes disregard into technical impossibility; intrusive line breaks remain.

adjudicated.jp: 同じ主人公なのに、違う人間なんだと思って、プレイした。
adjudicated.en:
I thought while playing that while he was the
same protagonist, he was yet a different human.
comments: Also that Tanaka ripped it off, but, well, the We Die Between Sleep And Waking Up is a very old cliche' it seems. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ゲームは難易度ばかりが高い、バランスの取れていないもので。
adjudicated.en:
The game had nothing to it but a high level of
difficulty, and there was simply no balance.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: けど鮮烈な死のイメージがつきまとい、俺は憑かれたように遊び続けた。
adjudicated.en:
But I kept playing as if possessed, chasing
after that striking image of death.
comments: Taichi likes to chase beautiful images, however difficult they are to obtain, even in videogames... except he conveniently forgets to mention how the game came with a complete walkthrough, doesn't he now. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The vivid image of death haunts or follows him, while he continues playing as if possessed. The English instead makes him voluntarily pursue that image and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text:
But I kept playing as if possessed, chasing
after that striking image of death.

adjudicated.jp: 結末は特攻オチだった。
adjudicated.en: Final punchline was a Bolivian Army Ending.
comments: The game's Phantasy Star II. PS2 is most famous for having one of the earliest cases of a major party character irreversibly die, which means Tanak~~ Taichi would be one of the very few people fascinated with what is an almost trivial detail all things considered. But it's consistent with his sometimes odd conclusions, see CCA0015C, CCD2002. I don't think there's a less tropistic way of saying this as quickly. There's additional material in Japan that changes this BAE, but it's nowhere near well known so its impact can be neglected here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 特攻オチ directly says the ending culminated in a suicidal or desperate special attack. The English substitutes a named Western media trope whose scope and mechanics are not necessarily identical.

adjudicated.jp: 「……げんなりだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...so dejecting."
adjudicated.assessment: げんなり describes being weary, disgusted, or thoroughly put off. 'Dejecting' is an unnatural participial adjective for his state.

adjudicated.jp: 自分がそれを体験するとは思わなかった。
adjudicated.en: I didn't think I would experience that myself.
comments: And this explication is made through videogames. Especially considering how he likes to act Main Character-like. And those, of course, have memory loss. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: してみると俺は何人目なのだろうか。
adjudicated.en: If that's how it is then, I am which number of myself now?
adjudicated.assessment: He wonders which iteration or number he is. The interrogative phrase cannot serve as the predicate after 'I am' in this word order.

highlights.text: I am which number of myself now?

adjudicated.jp: 五人目。
adjudicated.en: Number five.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 果たして本当にそうなのか。
adjudicated.en: Is that truly what I am, really?
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 記録になければ、それを知る手だてはないのだ。
adjudicated.en: If there are no records, then there is no way to know that.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
